_about: Eras of transistor structure. feature_nm is the characteristic lateral dimension of the day (contact spacing, then drawn gate length, then the marketing node label). 'arch' selects the cross-section drawn by sim/transistor_sim/crosssection.py and the 3D explorer.

eras.title: Point-contact transistor
eras.who: John Bardeen & Walter Brattain, Bell Labs
eras.summary: Two gold foil contacts pressed onto a germanium slab a fraction of a millimetre apart. Current injected at one contact modulated current at the other: the first solid-state amplifier.
eras.structure: Gold contacts on a plastic wedge pressed into n-type Ge; base contact on the back.

eras.title: Grown-junction bipolar transistor
eras.who: William Shockley, Morgan Sparks, Gordon Teal
eras.summary: Shockley's junction theory (1949) replaced fragile point contacts with a thin p-type base sandwiched between n-type emitter and collector, grown into the crystal.
eras.structure: n-p-n layers grown in a single crystal; base width tens of micrometres.

eras.title: First commercial silicon transistor
eras.summary: Silicon kept working at temperatures where germanium leaked. TI's grown-junction silicon transistors opened military and industrial markets.
eras.structure: Grown-junction n-p-n silicon.

eras.title: Oxide masking and the planar process
eras.summary: Thermally grown SiO2 masks dopant diffusion and stays on to protect the junctions. Every transistor is now made flat, from the top, by photolithography.
eras.structure: Diffused base and emitter windows opened in oxide; aluminium contacts on top.

eras.title: Integrated circuit
eras.summary: Kilby put a transistor, capacitor and resistors on one germanium chip with flying gold wires. Noyce's planar version wired them with evaporated aluminium over oxide, which is how every chip since is built.
eras.structure: Multiple planar devices on one die, isolated by junctions, connected by aluminium over oxide.

eras.title: MOSFET
eras.who: Mohamed Atalla & Dawon Kahng, Bell Labs
eras.summary: A metal gate over thermally grown oxide controls a surface channel. The field-effect idea (Lilienfeld 1925, Heil 1934) finally worked because the Si/SiO2 interface was clean.
eras.structure: Al gate on ~100 nm SiO2 over p-Si with n+ source and drain.

eras.title: Complementary MOS (CMOS)
eras.summary: Pair an n-channel and a p-channel device so one is always off: near-zero standby power. It took 20 years to win, and it still runs almost every digital chip.
eras.structure: nMOS in p-substrate, pMOS in an n-well, sharing input and output.

eras.title: Self-aligned silicon gate
eras.summary: A polysilicon gate survives the high-temperature source/drain diffusion, so it masks its own junctions. Overlap capacitance falls and density doubles; the Intel 4004 (1971) used it.
eras.structure: Doped poly-Si gate defines source/drain edges automatically.

eras.title: Dennard scaling
eras.summary: Shrink every dimension and voltage by the same factor k and power density stays constant while speed rises. This rule drove 30 years of free performance.
eras.structure: Ion-implanted 1 µm MOSFET design used as the worked example.

eras.title: VLSI CMOS
eras.summary: CMOS overtakes nMOS as chips pass a quarter-million transistors. Scalable λ-based design rules and SPICE simulation make VLSI design a discipline.
eras.structure: Twin-well CMOS, LOCOS isolation, one or two aluminium layers.

eras.title: Deep sub-micron & copper
eras.summary: Shallow-trench isolation, lightly doped drains, silicided contacts and copper wiring. The wires begin to matter as much as the transistors.
eras.structure: STI, LDD spacers, CoSi2/NiSi contacts, 6+ copper layers.

eras.title: Strained silicon
eras.summary: Stretching or squeezing the silicon lattice speeds up electrons and holes. Embedded SiGe source/drain compresses pMOS channels; nitride caps stretch nMOS.
eras.structure: Recessed SiGe S/D for pMOS, tensile SiN liner for nMOS.

eras.title: High-k metal gate
eras.summary: SiO2 had thinned to about five atomic layers and leaked badly. Hafnium oxide gives the same capacitance with a physically thicker film; metal gates end poly depletion.
eras.structure: HfO2 gate dielectric, work-function metal, replacement-metal-gate flow.

eras.title: FinFET / Tri-gate
eras.summary: Stand the channel up as a fin and wrap the gate over three sides. Better electrostatic control brings subthreshold swing back toward 60 mV/decade and cuts leakage.
eras.structure: Si fins ~8 nm wide and ~40 nm tall, gate on three sides.

eras.title: EUV lithography in production
eras.who: ASML NXE:3400 at TSMC N7+ / Samsung 7LPP
eras.summary: 13.5 nm light from tin-plasma sources replaces multi-patterned 193 nm immersion for the tightest layers.
eras.structure: FinFET with EUV-printed contacts and vias.

eras.title: Gate-all-around nanosheets
eras.who: Samsung SF3E (2022); TSMC N2 & Intel 18A RibbonFET (HVM Q4 2025)
eras.summary: Stack three or four horizontal silicon sheets and surround each with gate. Sheet width can be tuned per cell, and the gate controls the channel from every side.
eras.structure: 3-4 Si sheets ~5 nm thick, inner spacers, gate on four sides.

eras.title: Backside power delivery
eras.who: Intel PowerVia (18A, 2025); TSMC A16 Super Power Rail (2H 2026)
eras.summary: Move the power wires under the transistors, to the back of a thinned wafer. Signal wires get the front side to themselves and voltage droop falls.
eras.structure: Nanosheets with power rails and contacts reached from the wafer backside.

eras.title: IBM 0.7 nm (7 Å) nanostack
eras.summary: IBM stacks and staggers nanosheet transistors vertically, claiming nearly twice the density of its 2 nm chip and up to 50% more performance or 70% better efficiency. It is a research node; IBM projects commercialization within about five years.
eras.structure: Vertically stacked, laterally staggered nFET/pFET nanosheets with backside bitlines for SRAM.

eras.title: 2D channels & the 0.42 nm interface
eras.who: NYCU & TSMC Corporate Research (Nature Electronics, Aug 2026); Fudan RV32-WUJI (Nature, 2025)
eras.summary: The '0.42 nm' result is the thickness of an oxidized-aluminium buffer between a one-molecule-thick MoS2 channel and its HfO2 gate dielectric, not a process node. It reached ~1 nm equivalent oxide thickness with low leakage and 0.45 mS/µm peak transconductance at ~100 nm channel length.
eras.structure: Top-gate FET: MoS2 (0.7 nm) / AlOx (0.42 nm) / HfO2 / metal gate.

eras.title: Forksheet, CFET and beyond
eras.summary: Forksheets put a dielectric wall between n and p sheets; CFETs stack pFET on nFET. Roadmaps extend to 'A5'-'A2' labels, where 2D channels may take over from silicon.
eras.structure: pFET nanosheets stacked directly above nFET nanosheets with a shared gate.
